clue.text: Responsible for worker being late

parts.note: to be behind something is to be responsible for it, as with the person behind a plan
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Someone blames a member of staff for turning up late.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand is an adjective meaning in arrears or behind schedule, so tardy.

clue.text: Will a department show this to do a U-turn?

definitions.text: Will a department show this to do a U-turn?

parts.words: Will a department show this to do a U-turn?
parts.note: doing a U-turn means reversing a stated position; the question pictures an official body retreating from a policy, cycling the other way

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a two-part word meaning to retreat from an earlier position; the clue imagines a department literally pedalling in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse or retract a previous stance is the idiomatic figurative sense, drawn from pedalling a bicycle in reverse.

clue.text: Abandoned child said to get traditional gift

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard rather than read, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: Hansel, with his sister Gretel, is left in the forest in the Grimm fairy tale

explanation.surface: A child left behind is supposedly given a customary present.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsel is an old customary gift marking a new year or a new venture, given for luck.

clue.text: Valley in which liquid dirt's covered rock structure

indicators.note: in which says the valley word receives the other piece within itself

parts.note: a dene is a narrow wooded valley

indicators.note: liquid suggests something fluid and changeable, so the letters of dirt are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A valley floor is coated with runny mud over a rock formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' rearranges DIRT to DRIT; 'covered' reads as part of the definition's picture but is just a link, the rock formation being the true definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dendrite is a branching, tree-like mineral pattern formed on or in rock, a rock structure.

clue.text: News agency processes data and is seen to be wrong

indicators.note: if the words are wrong as they stand, their letters must be put right by rearranging

explanation.surface: A wire service handles information and is found to be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be wrong' rearranges PROCESSES DATA IS into the agency's name; 'and' and 'seen' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Associated Press is a major American news-gathering cooperative supplying stories to newspapers.

clue.text: Parachute beginning to drop, one out of line with others

indicators.note: beginning to picks only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.words: one out of line with others
parts.note: a rogue is an individual that behaves differently from the rest of its group, like a rogue elephant

explanation.surface: Something about a parachute starting to fall with one canopy out of step.
explanation.definitionFit: A drogue is a small parachute used to slow or stabilise a craft or to pull out a main parachute.

clue.text: Brass making harsh noise getting left out

indicators.note: getting something out means removing it, so the abbreviation for left is taken away

parts.note: a clash is a loud discordant sound

explanation.surface: Brass instruments produce a racket when one side drops out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like the band's section producing the noise, but it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is informal British slang for money, as in muck and brass.

clue.text: Cold air restricting summer gala? Enter this for refreshment

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: restricting suggests holding something in, so the song word encloses the festival

parts.note: an aria is an air or melody sung solo in opera
a fete is an outdoor fund-raising fair, typically held in summer

explanation.surface: Chilly weather limits an outdoor fair, so go inside for a drink instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' wants to be the weather, but it is the operatic song. A British fete is a village fair with stalls and games, held outdoors in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service eating place that one enters to get food and drink.

clue.text: Country fellow is trapping game the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards, so the whole assembled string is reversed

parts.note: a man is a fellow, a chap

indicators.note: trapping says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
RU stands for rugby union, a ball game

explanation.surface: A man in some country catches wild animals in a muddled fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: IS holds RU to give IRUS; MAN + IRUS read in reverse gives the country's older spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Surinam, also spelt Suriname, is a country on the north-east coast of South America.

clue.text: Study openings in religious communities

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart, an old sense
vents are openings that let air or gas out

explanation.surface: Someone examines the apertures in monasteries and nunneries.
explanation.definitionFit: Convents are houses of nuns or monks, communities living under religious vows.

clue.text: Individual collects wood for burning

indicators.note: collects suggests gathering something in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: one means a single individual
fir is a softwood timber from conifer trees

explanation.surface: A person gathers timber to make a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on fire is to be ablaze, actively burning.

clue.text: Job providing type of support

definitions.meaning: an upright pole or stake that holds something up

explanation.definitionFit: Post means both a position of employment and an upright supporting pole or stake.

clue.text: Describing activity in a close election

definitions.meaning: giving an account of events, narrating them
when the result is very tight, the votes are tallied a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Recounting means both narrating an account and counting votes again after a tight result.

clue.text: Daughter's animal at play?

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

indicators.note: at play suggests the letters frolicking about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl's pet romps around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges ANIMAL AT to ALMATIAN after D; the whole clue doubles as a picture of a family dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian is a spotted breed of dog, a typical family pet animal for a child.

clue.text: Someone like Tom Thumb could be called up at short notice

definitions.meaning: a tiny person, read as a man who is minute in size

definitions.text: could be called up at short notice
definitions.meaning: an American Revolutionary militiaman ready to fight within a minute's warning

explanation.definitionFit: Minutemen were colonial militia ready instantly; read literally it is a very small man.

clue.text: Stuff at front of picnic hamper

parts.note: to cram is to stuff or pack tightly

indicators.note: front of takes just the leading letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Food is packed at the top of a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a picnic basket, but it is the verb meaning restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to restrict or hinder, the verb sense of hamper.

clue.text: It's appropriate to be lively and attractive in hospital department

parts.note: pert means sprightly and neatly attractive
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A nurse is said to suit a cheerful, pretty manner in her ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent means relevant to the matter in hand, so apt or fitting.

clue.text: Like some dishes of the month with grass in!

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August
to grass is to inform, and a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: Some food is a seasonal speciality with lawn clippings stirred in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like lawn, but it is slang for an informer, a RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Au gratin describes dishes topped with browned breadcrumbs or cheese.

clue.text: Port kept in cellar necessarily

indicators.note: kept in signals the answer is held within the following words

explanation.surface: A bottle of fortified wine must stay in the wine cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine kept in a cellar, but it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Larne is a ferry port town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Receptacle not in the right place outside front of house

indicators.note: outside says the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: astray means off course, out of position

indicators.note: front of takes just the leading letter of house

explanation.surface: A container has been misplaced and left out by the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is a dish that receives cigarette ash, a receptacle.

clue.text: Supervisor heads for the office in uniform

indicators.note: in places the picked letters within the other word

parts.note: regular means uniform, evenly consistent

indicators.note: heads for takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A manager makes for the office wearing a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing, but here it is the adjective meaning consistent.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator is a person or body that supervises and controls an activity.

clue.text: After end of breakfast worker on oil platform set off

indicators.note: end of takes only the final letter of the word

parts.note: a rigger works on an oil rig

explanation.surface: Once breakfast is finished, an oil-rig hand heads out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the rigger after T, matching the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger is to set off, as with an alarm or a chain of events.

clue.text: Began as writer in huge lexicographical enterprise

indicators.note: in places the writing implement within the dictionary

parts.note: the OED, the Oxford English Dictionary, is a vast dictionary project
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: Someone started as an author on a vast dictionary project.
explanation.definitionFit: Opened means began or started, as in opened the meeting.

clue.text: Sort of official report that's eschewed by the FT

definitions.text: Sort of official report that's eschewed by the FT

parts.words: Sort of official report that's eschewed by the FT
parts.note: a government policy document, here linked to the Financial Times being printed on salmon-pink newsprint and so avoiding the usual paper colour

explanation.walkthrough: The FT, the Financial Times, is famously printed on pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A government policy document is called by a name that literally describes pale, unprinted newsprint.

clue.text: Note shortened type of garment

indicators.note: shortened says the word loses its end

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

explanation.surface: A memo is cut down about a kind of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' cuts the last M from MINIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt or dress, a type of garment.

clue.text: State allows this person to keep gun? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: to keep says one piece holds the other
quite the opposite reverses who holds whom, so the gun holds the person

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun
me is how the setter refers to themselves

explanation.surface: A state lets someone own a firearm, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' is a German federal state, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bremen is one of the sixteen states of Germany, a city-state.

clue.text: Lean gent could be seen as catch

indicators.note: could be seen as suggests the letters may be viewed in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A thin man might be regarded as a good match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' looks like a desirable partner, but it is the verb to snare.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to snare or trap, so to catch.

clue.text: City simply moving couple to the front

indicators.note: a couple means two letters, here the last two, carried to the start

parts.note: only means simply or merely

explanation.surface: A town where a pair just relocates to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyon is a major French city on the Rhone and Saone.

clue.text: Cut out item of food around home -—— get sick when it returns

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a dish is a prepared item of food
in means at home

indicators.note: returns means coming back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: to tire of something is to get sick of it

explanation.surface: Someone cuts out a food item at home and feels ill afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out' wants to be a literal snip, but it means removing someone from a will; 'when it returns' turns TIRE into ERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinherit is to cut someone out of a will.
